add_ons.name: Knowledge search
add_ons.summary: Lets an agent answer from your own documents, not only from what it already knows.
add_ons.example: A grant reviewer asks what the policy says about travel. The agent finds the right passage and names where it came from.
add_ons.pilot: Ask Checklist and case helper to use the sample policy guidance when it summarizes case notes. It looks up ten approved sample passages and names the one it used. Your own documents cannot be added yet.
cost: The search service is billed by the hour while it runs. The price depends on its size.
Ranking results by meaning and preparing documents for search add small extra charges.
The pilot runs on the search service the platform already has, so it adds no new hourly charge.
needs: A search service on the private network.
Your documents, kept in storage you control.
add_ons.safety: Only documents added on purpose can be searched, and access is read-only through a managed identity, not keys.
add_ons.billing: Search units per hour by tier, plus semantic ranker and embedding calls.
add_ons.note: The pilot (#122) runs on the dev platform's Basic search service (#76) with one index of ten sample passages. Decide the tier before anything larger.

add_ons.name: Conversation memory
add_ons.summary: Lets an agent remember earlier conversations, so people do not have to repeat themselves.
add_ons.example: A returning person carries on with an earlier case without restating the details.
cost: Billed for how much the database is used, either as reserved capacity or per request.
Stored conversations also add a storage charge.
needs: A decision on how long conversations are kept.
A way to delete the history of anyone who asks.
add_ons.safety: It would store what people type, so it needs retention and deletion rules before it is used.
add_ons.billing: Provisioned or serverless request units, plus storage.

add_ons.name: Document extraction
add_ons.summary: Lets an agent read scanned forms, receipts and PDFs, so it can work with the text and fields in them.
add_ons.example: An expense claim arrives as a photo of a receipt. The agent reads the date and the total from it.
cost: Billed for each page that is read.
needs: A person checks anything the reader is unsure about.
add_ons.safety: It would read documents only inside your private network, and it would not keep them unless you decide it should.

add_ons.name: Notifications
add_ons.summary: Lets an agent send a message once a person has approved it.
add_ons.example: The agent drafts an email to a vendor. A person reads it, then chooses Send.
cost: Billed for each message sent, or for each step when the message goes through a workflow.
needs: A sender address your organization owns.
A named person who approves every message.
add_ons.safety: The agent only drafts. A person must approve every send, and nothing goes out on its own.
add_ons.service: Azure Communication Services email, or Logic Apps
add_ons.billing: Per message, or per action for Logic Apps.

add_ons.name: Code interpreter
add_ons.summary: Lets an agent run small calculations on the data you give it, instead of doing the arithmetic in its head.
add_ons.example: The agent totals the lines on an expense claim and shows its working.
cost: Billed for each session the agent opens.
needs: Nothing to set up in the Lab. It is a built-in Foundry tool.
add_ons.safety: It runs in a sandbox managed by Foundry and only sees the data it is given.
add_ons.service: Foundry Agent Service code interpreter tool
add_ons.note: Prefer the tools Foundry already provides over rebuilding them in the Lab.

add_ons.name: Web search
add_ons.summary: Lets an agent look things up on the public internet.
add_ons.example: The agent checks a current public regulation before it answers.
cost: Charged for each search by the search provider. The price has not been assessed yet.
needs: Explicit approval of what may be sent outside your organization.
add_ons.safety: The questions the agent asks would leave your organization and go to a public search service.
